ali: Quick check — onboarded quartz-v1 (fp16) -> int8 (symmetric per-channel). Short-query holdout shows recall@5 drop 0.79 -> 0.65. Noticed cluster tightness change too. Anyone free to eyeball?

grace: can you paste the eval command and config?

ali: eval command: ```bash
python eval/recall.py --model quartz-v1 --quant int8_sym --holdout short-queries.csv --k 5 --batch 256 --norm l2 --whiten true
```

deni: initial thought: symmetric quant can struggle with skewed channel distributions. did you try percentile clipping or asymmetric quant?

ali: tried clip 99.0 -> recall@5 0.68. per-tensor quant was worse (0.61). no asymmetric yet.

ci-bot: run queued on eval-2. job id 90210.

(40s later) ci-bot: run 90210 finished. metrics: fp16 recall@5=0.79, int8_sym_clip99=0.68, int8_asym_perchannel=0.76. cluster-silhouette: fp16 0.45 -> int8_sym 0.36 -> int8_asym 0.42. flagged: short-query recall delta > 0.05.

grace: asym per-channel almost recovers it. what's the cost impact?

ali: asym adds +2% model storage, negligible throughput change. tradeoff seems fine for short-query cohorts.

deni: can we automate a quick sensitivity probe during onboarding: compute per-dim mse fp16->quant and if top-k dims explain > 20% of reconstruction error, recommend asym or hybrid fallback?

grace: yes; add small heuristic and a note in onboarding checklist. also add a unit test to fail the quant job if recall@5 delta > 0.06 on short-queries without asym/hybrid.

ali: I'll update the onboarding doc and raise INF-7310 to wire the probe + unit test. attaching run ids: runs/quartz_fp16.json, runs/quartz_int8_sym_clip99.json, runs/quartz_int8_asym.json

grace: thanks — let's also run a multilingual short-holdout later (FR/ES) before we sign off.

deni: noted. closing for now, tracked by INF-7310. :white_check_mark:
